title: Adaptive burst anchoring and cross-plan soft-fallbacks PRD
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: provide a predictable yet flexible burst model for customers who have spiky traffic patterns, while preventing surprise overage charges and reducing operational overhead for billing support. This PRD outlines an 'anchored burst' construct (a reservable baseline burst allowance tied to a plan) plus an automated cross-plan soft-fallback mechanism that re-routes excess short-term demand to linked fallback credit pools or cheaper model variants without immediate billing spikes. The feature should minimize manual plan changes, reduce support tickets from burst-related billing surprises, and keep high-priority routes available during transients.
background: We have frequent support escalations where customers experience sharp traffic spikes (cron jobs, product launches, marketing campaigns) and receive large overage invoices or are abruptly throttled. Current options (hard quotas, manual plan bumps, or one-off credits) either create billing unpredictability or manual toil. Existing billing artifacts cover many quota and tier behaviors, but none provide a first-class, automated burst fallback that preserves per-route SLAs while controlling cost exposure.
proposed_solution: Introduce two cooperating mechanisms: 1) Anchored Burst Allowance: each plan includes an explicit 'burst anchor' (X token-minutes per billing window) that is consumption-exempt from immediate overage for short windows (configurable sliding window, default 10 minutes). Anchors are priced into plans as a stable delta. 2) Cross-Plan Soft-Fallbacks: customers can designate fallback pools (e.g., lower-cost sandbox plan, pooled enterprise reserve, or assigned burst credits) that are consumed when anchors are exhausted. Soft-fallbacks apply policy-controlled degradations: non-critical routes (analytics embeddings, background batch jobs) are routed to cheaper model variants or a throttled path; critical routes preserve latency by consuming fallback credits. Policy rules include prioritization, max fallback consumption per hour, and automatic notifications when fallback thresholds are hit. Billing behavior: anchor usage is not billed as overage; fallback consumption is billed at the fallback pool rate and included in the next invoice with clear line-item labeling. Admins can opt into auto-refill rules, alerts, and automatic conversion of heavy fallback use into a temporary reserved capacity offer.
scope_inclusions: - Plan schema changes to include 'burst_anchor' value and 'anchor_window' default.- Billing line item generation for anchor usage and fallback consumption.- Policy engine to evaluate route criticality and decide when to route to fallback.- UI in Console for admins to configure fallback pools, anchor sizing, and alerting thresholds.- API extensions for programmatic opt-in/opt-out of fallback and anchor overrides by account owners.
scope_exclusions: - Changes to underlying GPU autoscaling or Dedicated capacity scheduling beyond billing-visible routing decisions.- Automated cross-customer credit borrowing (not allowed for privacy/compliance). - Complex ML-driven predictive resizing in initial rollout (can be a future enhancement).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta, billing sandbox): implement anchor usage tracking and a developer-facing sandbox fallback pool; enable per-tenant opt-in and logs-only mode for 4 weeks. Phase 2 (Controlled GA): enable billing line items for anchors and fallback consumption for a subset of production accounts and surface Console controls; collect metrics and feedback for 6 weeks. Phase 3 (Full GA): enable auto-refill and reserved capacity offers, add REST API endpoints for programmatic control, and publish docs and migration guides.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Anchors are included in plan metadata and surfaced in Console and Plan API for all affected plans.
AC2: Anchor consumption is tracked with per-tenant granularity and exported to billing pipeline as distinct line items (anchor-usage, fallback-usage).
AC3: Cross-plan fallback routing can be configured via Console and API; fallback routing decisions obey route-level criticality rules and do not change request semantics.

AC4: When anchor is exhausted, critical routes continue with fallback credits (if available) and non-critical routes are downgraded according to configured policies; no silent hard-throttling occurs without prior admin opt-in.

AC5: Billing math must be validated end-to-end: invoices reflect anchor pricing, fallback unit rates, and any auto-refill charges; sample invoices for 3 synthetic spike scenarios must match expected calculations.
AC6: Alerts (Console and email) are sent when anchor utilization reaches 70%, 90%, and when fallback consumption surpasses configured hourly limits.
AC7: Performance: fallback decisions add no more than 2ms median request overhead in the routing path for 99% of requests in test harness.
AC8: Documentation and migration guide published; support playbook created and validated with Support team for common customer questions and invoice disputes.

qa_plan: Create synthetic spike scenarios (small: 10x baseline for 15 min, medium: 50x for 5 min, large: 100x for 2 min) across three tenant profiles (startup, scale-up, enterprise). Validate routing behavior, fallback consumption, line-item generation, and SLA preservation for critical routes. Automate end-to-end tests in staging billing pipeline and run cost-reconciliation jobs against golden calculations.
